text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A witness tells a commission investigating student unrest at the country's two universities drug and alcohol abuse among students are to blame for their riotous behaviour.
- Zambia Concrete, a state-run company based in central Zambia, retrenches 91 workers.
- Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines says it is willing to give up an agricultural settlement scheme in central Zambia to the government.
- The state-run Zambia Electricity Supply Corp (Zesco) says it has spent $2 million in a network information and planning system project to improve power distribution in the capital.
- President Frederick Chiluba appoints former finance deputy minister Koshita Shengamo as high commissioner to Namibia, replacing incumbent Chanda Sosala.
- Bailiffs seize seven coffins from a funeral parlour owing another company around $3,000.
